title: Scotland · Applecross, Torridon and West Coast
slogan: A 224 km loop out of Lochcarron
story: Big sky, single-track discipline and one of Britain’s great rider days. This road trip is shaped as a ride, not as a shortcut: leave the start cleanly, use the first checkpoint for fuel and weather discipline, then let the middle 90 km be the part you remember. The best part sits around Bealach na Bà, Torridon mountain view, while Lochcarron fuel gate and Applecross lunch coast keep the day practical instead of turning it into a fuel hunt. Check the selected map before departure: scenic sections, transfer sections, speed/control reminders, risk points and the GPX checkpoint order are deliberately visible so the route is understandable before the engine starts. Ride it early if the area is popular, keep the photo stops legal, and shorten the route if weather, daylight or energy stops agreeing with the plan.

scenicChapters.title: North Coast 500
scenicChapters.narrative: Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did. Water arrives beside the road and stays for 46 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go.

scenicChapters.title: A82 Glencoe and Great Glen
scenicChapters.narrative: For 23 km this is A82 Glencoe and Great Glen, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.
